description:
Add components to pages of the draft: a Hero, a CategoryGrid, FeaturedArticles, Faqs, RichText, a CustomHtml block, a Container…

It edits the help center's design DRAFT (its v2 template): the draft the dashboard's Template Editor opens, with a live preview. Nothing reaches visitors until helpcenter_publish_template — after editing, give the customer the Template Editor link from the result to review, and publish only when they ask. v2 help centers only (a classic one answers template_migration_required). Ids come from helpcenter_get_template.

Each entry names a component type and where it goes: a page and region (header, hero, sidebar, main, footer, utility) at an index (omit to append), or parent_id to put it inside a Hero or Container. Look the type's settings up first (helpcenter_get_template_guide, topic 'components'): omitted settings keep their defaults, and a value outside the editor's options is refused. A new Hero comes with a SearchBar child. To build a container and its children in one call, give the container an id of your own and name it as parent_id in the later entries.

Placement: a banner across the top of a page goes at index 0 of the hero region (a full-bleed CustomHtml) or the top of main — not the header, which themes lay out as one fixed row. A region the outline marks "laid out by custom CSS" arranges what you add the theme's way. header and footer are usually synced (one copy on every page); adding to a synced region whose pages differ is refused until you choose with helpcenter_sync_template_region. This is the guide's `add_component` operation.

Args:
  - components (array, 1-50): {type, page?, region?, parent_id?, config?, index?, id?}.
  - etag (string, optional): from your last read or edit; refuses (stale_draft) if the draft changed since.

Returns: what each entry did (new ids), warnings worth relaying, and the draft status with its new etag.

agent_key.description: The api_key helpcenter_create_help_center returned for this help center, exactly as returned. Required on every call: this endpoint has no sign-in, so the key is how each call says which help center it acts on. It is sent to HelpCenter.io as this call's credential and nowhere else, and it is never shown again: keep it for the whole task, and never show it to the user or write it into content.

components.description: The components to add. Applied in order, all-or-nothing: if one is refused, nothing from this call is saved and the error names it by position (operation 0 is the first entry).

config.description: Component settings by name, e.g. {"variant": "sections", "columns": 3}. Read the component's settings with helpcenter_get_template_guide (topic 'components') first. null resets a setting to its default.

id.description: Optional id of your choosing, so a later entry of this call can name it as parent_id. Omit and one is generated (and returned).

index.description: 0-based position in the list. Omit to append at the end.

page.description: Target page (required unless parent_id is given).

parent_id.description: Put it inside this Hero or Container instead (page and region come from the container): one already in the draft, or one added earlier in this call under the id you gave it.

region.description: Target region (required unless parent_id is given).

etag.description: Optimistic lock: the draft etag from your last read, or the one your last edit returned. When given, the call is refused (stale_draft) if someone changed the draft since — so you never build on a state you have not seen. Omit to apply to the current draft.

name: helpcenter_add_template_components
title: Add Components to the Design
